claims.statement: Verified fact: the Ministry of Finance publishes KSeF 2.0 API documentation for integration with external financial-accounting systems, and the production API was made available in January 2026.
Verified fact: Polish split payment separates the net and VAT amounts, and the Ministry provides a technical flat-file mechanism for bulk checking VAT-listed accounts.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): accounting firms will pay for a cross-system exception ledger because invoice availability alone does not complete payment reconciliation or the close.

contrary_evidence: The Ministry explicitly supports integration by commercial financial-accounting software, so incumbent suites are the obvious substitute: https://www.gov.pl/web/finanse/publikacja-dokumentacji-api-ksef-20-oraz-struktury-logicznej-fa3

PSD2 account-information providers are regulated and centrally registered, making an unlicensed direct bank-data strategy unsafe: https://www.eba.europa.eu/risk-and-data-analysis/data/registers/payment-institutions-register

economics.acquisition_route: Founder-led pilots with 2-3 Warsaw or Wielkopolska accounting offices, followed by referrals and implementation-partner revenue share; no camera-led audience required.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 15 offices at PLN 3,000 MRR by year 2, 50 at PLN 4,000 MRR by year 4, and 90 at PLN 4,500 MRR by year 6 imply about PLN 4.86m ARR. At 25% owner earnings and a 3-4x ARR valuation, 70% founder ownership could exceed PLN 5m net worth in years 5-7; failure to reach 20 repeat offices by month 30 invalidates this path.
economics.founder_time: 3-4 hours/day until five pilots; automate onboarding and use a contractor for connector maintenance while retaining the full-time job.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 78-88% software gross margin after KSeF/bank connectors and support; manually investigated exceptions must be separately priced or capped.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: one avoided day of reconciliation work or one prevented payment-control error could repay a PLN 2,000-4,000 monthly fee; measure in a paid four-week pilot.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 1,500-6,000 per accounting office per month plus PLN 2-8 per exception above an included allowance.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every invoice cycle and statutory close repeats; accumulated matching rules, audit trails, and entity mappings make replacement costly.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a permissioned corpus of labeled Polish payment exceptions improves matching rules and creates workflow switching costs without monetizing raw client data
fingerprint.customer: Polish accounting offices serving 30-300 SMEs, and finance teams of Polish multi-entity groups
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: accounting-software implementers, bookkeeping associations, and a low-touch migration offer based on the firm's own exports
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: multi-tenant SaaS with KSeF ingestion, bank-feed matching, White List evidence snapshots, exception queues, and an immutable close packet; subscription plus exception volume
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the accounting firm or group finance lead pays a monthly portfolio fee when the close dashboard is delivered, with an optional fee for each exception resolved
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a month-end close in which KSeF invoices, partial payments, split payments, credit notes, and approved bank accounts do not reconcile automatically

founder_fit: Uses data science, entity matching, and AI-assisted exception classification.
Polish location and finance interest help with KSeF-specific discovery.
A CSV-first pilot is compatible with a five-hour daily cap and PLN 100,000 capital ceiling.
Partner-led distribution reduces continuous high-energy selling and personal-brand exposure.
risks: Handling tax and bank data creates a high security and GDPR burden.
Offering account-information services directly could require regulated status; the product must remain export-based or partner with a licensed provider.
Accounting suites may add adequate native matching quickly.
Incorrect compliance flags could create consequential customer reliance.

structure.control_point: canonical matched state between a structured tax invoice and its settlement evidence
structure.critical_dependency: delegated KSeF access plus reliable bank data through customer exports or a licensed PSD2 account-information provider

thesis: Build a read-only reconciliation layer for Polish accounting offices and multi-entity SMEs that binds each KSeF invoice to bank receipts, split-payment treatment, VAT-account status, and White List checks, then routes only unresolved exceptions to a human. The paid event is a completed monthly close or a resolved exception, not generic invoice storage. This is an unvalidated commercial hypothesis; the initial product would not initiate payments and would use exports or a licensed account-information partner.
title: KSeF-to-Cash Exception Ledger for Polish Accounting Firms
uncertainties: No evidence yet that accounting offices will pay separately rather than demand the feature from their existing suite.
The true frequency and cost of post-KSeF settlement exceptions is unknown.
KSeF delegated-access onboarding friction and commercial bank-feed pricing are untested.
The assumed sales cycle and attainable portfolio price are estimates, not commitments.
